 Update: Joel Embiid was able to return for the Philadelphia 76ers at the start of the second half after receiving treatment in the locker room. He did change his shoes during intermission, according to the broadcast.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement As the NBA world fixes their collective eyes on the City of Brotherly Love to see Jaylen Brown take on his former team, the Boston Celtics , disaster struck when Philadelphia 76ers center Joel Embiid limped to the locker room after taking a hard fall while trying to score on former teammate Paul George .
 While the play wasn't immediately called off, as the ball remained live for VJ Edgecombe to slam down a sick dunk – even if he had to then gingerly avoid his teammate on his way down from the rim – Embiid immediately beelined it right to the locker room when the clock hit zero for treatment.
 Transitioning into more of a supplemental piece for the 76ers in 2026 after a decade holding things down as their No. 1 option, Embiid's health has remained an issue to start the season, with the former MVP missing two of his team's first 11 games. Fortunately, when Embiid does play, he's remained very effective, putting more effort into defense as his teammates take some of the scoring burden off his plate.
 Click Here to Subscribe With Adem Bona dealing with injury concerns of his own and Dominik Barlow still out, hopefully Embiid is able to work out any discomfort and return to the game, as the options behind him aren't ideal for a team with NBA Championship ambitions.
